title: South Carolina Gold Mustard Barbecue Sauce
description: Bloomed yellow mustard seed, honey and cider vinegar make a mellow golden barbecue sauce with a little smoked paprika.

ingredients.name: table salt
ingredients.note: Fine table salt, about 590 mg sodium per 1/4 teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/16 tsp total.

steps.title: Bloom the mustard
steps.text: Whisk {ms} and {w} in the skillet. Let stand off heat for 4 minutes to bring out the mustard flavor.

steps.title: Mellow the gold sauce
steps.text: Whisk in {ac}, {ho}, {cv}, {pa}, {bs} and {salt}. Simmer gently for 6–7 minutes until the mustard loses its raw bite.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over pulled pork or sliced chicken. Serve a little extra on the side so the meat stays moist.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/16 tsp table salt in place of 1/4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, halve the vinegar and simmer the mustard 2 minutes longer. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 48 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 10.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.6 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 150 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 48 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 10.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.6 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 39 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
